quote: An abnormal increase of antimicrobial dual oxidase (DUOX2) expression was detected in association with an expansion of Proteobacteria in both UC and CD, while expression of lipoprotein APOA1 gene was downregulated and associated with CD-specific alterations in Firmicutes.
summary: DUOX2 expression is abnormally raised in ileal biopsies of treatment-naive pediatric UC and CD patients and tracks mucosal injury severity.

quote: Duox1 and Duox2 localize to the apical plasma membrane of epithelial cells in major airways, salivary glands, and the gastrointestinal tract, and provide extracellular hydrogen peroxide to lactoperoxidase to produce antimicrobial hypothiocyanite ions.
summary: Review of Nox/Duox oxidases in innate defense; Duox2 supplies epithelial hydrogen peroxide for antimicrobial activity.

quote: Recent evidence suggests that both NOX1 and DUOX2 species produce ROS in the gastrointestinal tract as a result of chronic inflammatory stress; cytokine induction (by interferon-γ, tumour necrosis factor α, and interleukins IL-4 and IL-13) of NOX1 and DUOX2 may contribute to the development of colorectal and pancreatic carcinomas in patients with inflammatory bowel disease and chronic pancreatitis, respectively.
summary: Review of NADPH oxidases in cancer, noting cytokine-induced DUOX2 ROS in the inflamed gut may contribute to colorectal cancer in IBD.

quote: More recently, additional diseases have been linked to functionally altered variants in genes encoding for other NADPH oxidases, such as for DUOX2/DUOXA2 in congenital hypothyroidism, or for the Nox2 complex, NOX1 and DUOX2 as risk factors for inflammatory bowel disease.
summary: Review of ROS-deficiency disorders listing DUOX2 variants as inflammatory bowel disease risk factors.

quote: DUOX2 regulates interactions between the intestinal microbiota and the mucosa to maintain immune homeostasis in mice.
summary: Duoxa knockout mice lack functional DUOX enzymes and show more bacterial access to lymphatic tissue and microbiota-driven immune responses, so DUOX2 supports mucosal homeostasis.

quote: This study identifies the first inactivating missense variants in NOX1 and DUOX2 associated with VEOIBD.
summary: Inactivating DUOX2 missense variants with reduced ROS production were found in very early onset IBD patients and impaired host resistance to infection, so loss of DUOX2 raises risk.

quote: Collectively, these data indicate that the gut microbiota uses two distinct signaling pathways to induce Duox2 expression in the ileum and colon epithelium.
summary: Gut microbiota induces Duox2 in mouse ileal and colonic epithelium through TRIF/NF-kB and MyD88/p38 pathways respectively.

quote: An integrative analysis identified colorectal cancer-related genes, including LCN2 and DUOX2, for which gene expression is correlated with the abundance of colorectal cancer-associated bacteria, such as Ruminococcaceae and Veillonella.
summary: DUOX2 expression correlates with certain bacteria in colonic mucosa of cystic fibrosis patients; not a UC study.

quote: Epithelial H2O2 was significantly increased in villin-TLR4 mice; TLR4-dependent tumorigenesis required the presence of DUOX2 and a microbiota.
summary: DUOX2 is up in IBD and colorectal cancer data; knocking out Duoxa in TLR4 mice reduced colitis-associated tumorigenesis.

quote: These findings indicate the nonredundant function of epithelial production of H2O2 in restricting microbial colonization.
summary: Duoxa knockout mice had greater Helicobacter felis gastric colonization and ineffective inflammation, so DUOX limits infection; a gastric not colonic model.

quote: DUOX2 with maturation partner DUOXA2 forms the predominant system for H2O2 production in human colon and is upregulated in active colitis.
summary: DUOX2 is epithelial, rises with inflammation in active UC biopsies, and is further increased by 5-ASA.

quote: In addition, 5-HT induced Nox2, p67(phox), and Duox2 without altering the level of Nox1 or Duox1 in colon epithelial cells, and silencing of Nox2 suppressed 5-HT-induced Duox2 increase.
summary: Serotonin raises Duox2 in colon epithelial cells via Nox2; Duox2 itself was not perturbed.

quote: The top ten upregulated genes were HMGCS2, UGT2A3 isoforms, B4GALNT2, MEP1B, GUCA2B, ADH1C, OTOP2, SLC9A3, and LYPD8; the top ten downregulated genes were PI3, DUOX2, VNN1, SLC6A14, GREM1, MMP1, CXCL1, TNIP3, TFF1, and LCN2.
summary: DUOX2 is among the top ten genes lower in long-duration than short-duration UC biopsies.

quote: Roles of several isoforms including DUOX1 and DUOX2 in host innate immune defense have been implicated and are still being uncovered.
summary: Review of antimicrobial functions of DUOX enzymes and lactoperoxidase, mainly in airway and salivary epithelium.

quote: Finally, the impact of DUOX2 variants on IL-17C induction provided a rationale for variant stratification in case control studies that substantiated DUOX2 as an IBD risk gene.
summary: Rare loss-of-function DUOX2 variants raise plasma IL-17C and increase IBD risk, and Duox2-deficient mice show higher intestinal Il17c.

quote: Nox1 and Duox2 are highly expressed in the gastrointestinal tract.
summary: Review of Nox/Duox enzymes in gastrointestinal immunopathology including IBD and H. pylori inflammation.

quote: Our results confirm in vivo the requirement of DUOXA for functional expression of DUOX-based reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidases and the role of DUOX isoenzymes as sole source of hormonogenic H(2)O(2).
summary: Duoxa knockout mice are severely hypothyroid; a thyroid study with no gut or inflammation outcome.

quote: TLR4 silencing with small interfering RNAs, as well as two independent NF-κB inhibitors, attenuated LPS- and IFN-γ-mediated Duox2 upregulation in BxPC-3 cells.
summary: IFN-gamma and LPS induce Duox2 through TLR4 and NF-kB in pancreatic cancer cells, and Duox is raised in chronic pancreatitis; not UC.

quote: Microbial dependent IL-17 signaling increases DUOX2 signaling in tumor cells.
summary: In a study of gut IL-17RA and distant tumors, microbe-dependent IL-17 signaling raises DUOX2 in tumor cells; unrelated to UC.

quote: Microarray analysis showed that of the 119 up-regulated genes in the J166WT-infected animals, several encode innate antimicrobial effector proteins, including elafin, siderocalin, DMBT1, DUOX2, and several novel paralogues of human-beta defensin-2.
summary: DUOX2 is one of several antimicrobial genes induced in macaque stomach by H. pylori; not UC.

quote: Analyzing 202,359 cells from 170 specimens across 83 patients, we identify a distinct epithelial cell type in both terminal ileum and ascending colon (hereon as 'LND') with high expression of LCN2, NOS2, and DUOX2 and genes related to antimicrobial response and immunoregulation.
summary: DUOX2 marks an expanded epithelial cell population (LND) in active Crohn's disease, linked to anti-TNF response.

quote: Exome sequencing identified candidate variants, including a missense mutation in DUOX2 that impaired its function and a frameshift mutation in CSF2RB that was associated with CD in an independent cohort of Ashkenazi Jewish individuals.
summary: Exome sequencing in Crohn's families found a DUOX2 missense variant that impaired H2O2 production, but it was not replicated as associated.

quote: Transcriptional profiling of the metabolically impaired epithelium reveals gene signatures involved in oxidative stress (Ido1, Nos2, Duox2).
summary: Duox2 is part of an oxidative stress signature in injured mouse epithelium that also distinguishes active Crohn's disease.

quote: Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), fluorescence-activated-cell-sorting, multiplex immunofluorescence (IF) and RNAscope analyses, we identified unique DUOX2+ACE2+ small cholangiocytes in human and mouse livers.
summary: DUOX2 marks a cholangiocyte subset that is reduced in primary biliary cholangitis; a liver study, not UC.

quote: Among the NOX family, the dual oxidases DUOX1 and DUOX2 are prominently expressed in epithelial cell types at mucosal surfaces and have therefore been considered to have important roles in innate host defence pathways.
summary: Review of DUOX enzymes in allergic disease that focuses on DUOX1 as the therapeutic target.
